profile.summary: RiNALMo is an RNA language model that reads an RNA sequence one nucleotide at a time and produces a numerical representation of each position. It was pretrained on 36 million non-coding RNA sequences by learning to fill in masked nucleotides, and the representations are then fine-tuned for tasks such as RNA secondary structure prediction and splice site prediction. The largest model has 650M parameters; smaller 148M and 33.5M versions are also released.

summary_quotes.text: In this work, each nucleotide is a single token.
RiNALMo-650M with 650M parameters, RiNALMo-150M with 148M parameters, and RiNALMo-33M with 33.5M parameters
RiNALMo is the largest RNA language model to date with 650 million parameters pre-trained on 36 million non-coding RNA sequences from several available databases.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: RiNALMo is an encoder-only transformer trained by masked language modelling: 15% of tokens in each training sequence are selected, most are replaced with a mask token, and the model learns to reconstruct them. It uses rotary position embeddings, SwiGLU feed-forward layers and FlashAttention-2. Training sequences were sampled once per cluster per epoch to keep batches diverse. For downstream use, the per-nucleotide representations or the classification token embedding feed a task head; the authors fine-tuned it for secondary structure prediction, splice site prediction, mean ribosome loading and ncRNA family classification.

quotes.text: To corrupt the input sequence, we randomly selected 15% of the tokens in the training sequence.
since we later sample from each cluster once per epoch
The position of the tokens is encoded using the RoPE
We provide pre-trained RiNALMo weights and fine-tuned weights for three downstream tasks: mean ribosome loading prediction, secondary structure prediction and splice-site prediction.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Three pretrained sizes are published on Zenodo: giga (650M), mega and micro. Their parameter counts differ slightly between the paper, the README and the Zenodo description. The 650M model was pretrained on seven 80 GB A100 GPUs for 2 weeks. Fine-tuned giga weights and the train_<task>.py scripts allow the paper's downstream evaluations to be rerun. The Python loader in the repository downloads only giga-v1. A result should name the size, whether pretrained or fine-tuned weights were used, and the Zenodo record (15043668).

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: RNA language model (BERT-style masked language model) that produces nucleotide representations for downstream RNA structure and function tasks.

quotes.text: We pre-trained RiNALMo using the MLM task where we corrupted unlabeled RNA sequences and then tasked the model to reconstruct them.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Encoder-only transformer. RiNALMo-650M (giga): 33 blocks, 1280-dimensional embeddings, 20 attention heads, feed-forward hidden size 3413, rotary position embeddings (RoPE), SwiGLU activation and FlashAttention-2. The repository configs give mega 30 blocks at 640 dimensions and micro 12 blocks at 480 dimensions, all with 20 heads.

quotes.text: Each multi-head attention has 20 attention heads.
The position of the tokens is encoded using the RoPE

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: RNA sequences, one token per nucleotide; U is replaced by T, and the vocabulary covers IUPAC nucleotide codes plus inosine.

quotes.text: In this work, each nucleotide is a single token. During tokenization, we replace all “U"s in the sequences with “T"s.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Per-nucleotide representations (the model output's "representation" field) and a classification token embedding; fine-tuned heads give secondary structure, splice site, mean ribosome loading and ncRNA family predictions.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: 36M unique non-coding RNA sequences, clustered into 17M clusters, from RNAcentral, nt, Rfam and Ensembl. Sequences shorter than 16 or longer than 8192 were removed, duplicates dropped, and the rest clustered with mmseqs easy-linclust (options --min-seq-id 0.7 and -c 0.8).

quotes.text: First, we collected noncoding RNA sequences from publicly available datasets RNAcentral, nt, Rfam and Ensembl. We removed sequences shorter than 16 and longer than 8192.
In the end, the dataset consisted of 36M unique ncRNA sequences clustered into 17M clusters.

facts.label: Known versions
facts.value: Three pretrained sizes on Zenodo (giga, mega, micro), plus giga models fine-tuned for secondary structure prediction (bpRNA and nine archiveII family splits), splice donor and acceptor prediction, mean ribosome loading and ncRNA family classification. The Python loader get_pretrained_model knows one name, giga-v1.

run_guide.summary: Install RiNALMo from the repository at a pinned commit and print nucleotide representations for two short RNA sequences with the 650M giga model.
prerequisites: Python 3.8 or later and CUDA 11.8 or later, as the README states, and a CUDA GPU (the example uses cuda:0). GPU memory needs are not stated.
Internet access: get_pretrained_model downloads the giga-v1 weights with gdown into ~/.cache/rinalmo_pretrained.
Code is Apache-2.0; weights are CC BY 4.0.

steps.title: Install
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/lbcb-sci/RiNALMo
cd RiNALMo
git checkout --detach 2c2c5c14a5ae609d8c560a5d9ca32e51e0288955
pip install .
pip install flash-attn==2.3.2
steps.explanation: The README's Quick Start installation, with a checkout line added to pin the commit this page read.

steps.title: Get nucleotide representations
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
import torch
from rinalmo.pretrained import get_pretrained_model

DEVICE = "cuda:0"

model, alphabet = get_pretrained_model(model_name="giga-v1")
model = model.to(device=DEVICE)
model.eval()
seqs = ["ACUUUGGCCA", "CCCGGU"]

tokens = torch.tensor(alphabet.batch_tokenize(seqs), dtype=torch.int64, device=DEVICE)
with torch.no_grad(), torch.cuda.amp.autocast():
  outputs = model(tokens)

print(outputs["representation"])
PY
steps.explanation: The README's Quick Start example, unchanged, wrapped in a shell heredoc. It downloads the giga-v1 weights on first use.

outputs: The tensor of nucleotide representations for the two input sequences, printed to the terminal.
